introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Commerce 2 (0520), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer FOUR questions. All questions carry equal marks.

Instructions: 1. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. 2. The use of SIMPLE electronic calculator is allowed. 3. Show clear working in your answer booklet where necessary.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde impose « Answer FOUR questions. All questions carry equal marks ». Le sujet imprime 6 questions, sans sections : `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné (2 pages : page de garde, puis les six questions sur une seule page) ; filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées. Les chiffres des exemples (FCFA) sont hypothétiques ; aucune statistique réelle, loi, taux ou institution n'est avancé au-delà des notions du programme.

Points : le sujet n'imprime que les points de chaque sous-question, jamais le total ; `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide. Pour chaque question les points imprimés totalisent 20 (Q1 : 8+6+6 ; Q2 : 6+6+8 ; Q3 : 6+8+6 ; Q4 : 8+8+4 ; Q5 : 6+8+6 ; Q6 : 8+8+4), conformément à « All questions carry equal marks » : aucun écart.

Question 4(a) : le sujet imprime « Amount (CFAF) » ; la devise est reprise telle quelle dans l'énoncé et traduite par FCFA dans le corrigé. « Working expenses » est interprété comme les charges d'exploitation déduites du bénéfice brut pour obtenir le bénéfice net. « Rate of turnover » est interprété comme le taux de rotation du stock = coût d'achat des marchandises vendues / stock moyen (50 000 / 15 000 = 3,33 fois) ; une lecture « chiffre d'affaires » (80 000) serait possible mais moins probable, car le sujet donne les deux stocks. Tous les résultats ont été recalculés avec Python (coût des ventes 50 000 ; bénéfice brut 30 000 ; bénéfice net 18 000 ; 22,5 % des ventes).

questions.enonce_markdown:
The information below are extracts from the trading, profits and loss accounts of a business at the end of a trading period.

| Particulars | Amount (CFAF) |
|---|---|
| Opening inventory | 20,000 |
| Closing inventory | 10,000 |
| Purchases | 40,000 |
| Sales | 80,000 |
| Working expenses | 12,000 |

You are required to calculate;

(i) gross profits,

(ii) net profits,

(iii) rate of turnover,

(iv) net profits as a percentage of sales.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Working (all amounts in FCFA, called CFAF in the question).**

**Step 1: cost of goods sold** = opening inventory + purchases - closing inventory

= 20,000 + 40,000 - 10,000 = **50,000**

**(i) Gross profit** = sales - cost of goods sold

= 80,000 - 50,000 = **30,000 FCFA**

**(ii) Net profit** = gross profit - working (operating) expenses

= 30,000 - 12,000 = **18,000 FCFA**

**(iii) Rate of turnover (stock turnover)** = cost of goods sold / average inventory

Average inventory = (opening inventory + closing inventory) / 2 = (20,000 + 10,000) / 2 = 15,000

Rate of turnover = 50,000 / 15,000 = 3.33, that is about **3.3 times** in the period. (This means that the stock was sold and replaced about three times; with a one-year period, a stock lasts about 365 / 3.33, that is about 110 days.)

**(iv) Net profit as a percentage of sales** = (net profit / sales) x 100

= (18,000 / 80,000) x 100 = **22.5 %**

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Gross profit | 30,000 FCFA |
| Net profit | 18,000 FCFA |
| Rate of turnover | 3.33 times |
| Net profit as % of sales | 22.5 % |

questions.enonce_markdown:
Name and briefly explain FOUR methods of advertising goods.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Advertising is any paid message that informs customers about goods and persuades them to buy. The main methods (media) are:

1. **Newspapers and magazines (the press).** Adverts are printed with words and pictures; they reach many readers, can be kept and read again, and a particular area or kind of reader can be targeted.
2. **Radio.** Spoken adverts and jingles reach a large audience, including people who cannot read, and are cheap; the message is short and cannot be seen.
3. **Television.** The advert combines sound, pictures and movement, so goods can be demonstrated and made very attractive, but air time is expensive.
4. **Posters and billboards.** Large printed messages are displayed along roads and in public places, where many people see them every day.
5. **Internet and social media.** Adverts are shown on websites and social networks and can be aimed at chosen groups of customers at low cost.
6. **Direct mail, leaflets and flyers.** Letters or leaflets are sent or handed directly to chosen customers, so the message is personal.
7. **Trade fairs and exhibitions, samples and in-store displays.** Customers can see, touch or test the goods before buying.

(Any four methods, each named and explained, earn full marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline any FOUR reasons why consumers need to be protected.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Consumer protection means safeguarding buyers' rights and interests. Consumers need protection for these reasons.

1. **Unsafe or poor-quality goods.** Some goods (food, drugs, electrical goods) can harm health if they are not properly made or have expired.
2. **False or misleading advertising.** Some sellers exaggerate or lie about the quality or price of goods.
3. **Unfair prices and hoarding.** Sellers may overcharge, especially when goods are scarce, or hide goods to raise prices.
4. **Wrong weights and measures and counterfeit (fake) goods.** Consumers can be cheated on quantity or sold imitations of known brands.
5. **Lack of information and knowledge.** Many consumers cannot test goods or understand technical details, so they depend on honest labelling.
6. **Weak bargaining power.** The individual buyer is weak compared with a big producer or monopoly, and has little chance of getting compensation without help.

(Any four reasons earn full marks.)
